data.name: v2.0.0
data.body:
> [!NOTE]
> Starting from version 2.0.0, we no longer provide builds of TrollStore JIT. You can package it yourself by following the [guide](https://github.com/Rednick16/TrollStoreJITEnabler).

This is a major release focused on a redesigned interface, expanded platform support, and advanced features. Landscape browsing, library management, and external controller navigation have been rebuilt. It also adds several new systems and brings Netplay to eligible Libretro cores.


### Before You Update

- Dreamcast (Flycast): Existing save states will no longer work as of 2.0.0. Convert important save states to in-game saves before updating, or back up the `Flycast/dc` folder yourself.
- Wii: A BootMii-format `keys.bin` is required.
- Symbian: Install firmware in Settings first (`.ROM`; S60v2 and later also need `.RPKG`).
- GameCube / Wii: The core is still being optimized, so heat and frame drops should still be expected.
- MAME: A number of lesser-used arcade systems have been trimmed. Some obscure titles may no longer run.

### Interface

Landscape

- A new landscape library, with most landscape pages redesigned.
- Built-in dynamic backgrounds. You can use or upload ShaderToy (GLSL) scripts to customize them. Only single-Image scripts are supported; complex scripts may increase battery use or heat.
- Multiple customizable card carousel styles.
- Focused background: when a game is selected, its banner can be used as the landscape focus backdrop.
- background music feature in landscape mode—besides built-in tracks, you can upload your own music files to use as background music.
- built in 12 sets of navigation and focus sound effects.

Game Options and Shortcuts

- A unified options list and interaction model throughout the app.
- Available actions are automatically arranged and regrouped for the current context.
- Advanced reordering: customize the order and grouping of options.
- A redesigned in-game shortcut menu. Shortcuts can appear on supported skins and in the in-game menu.

Navigation and Input

- A global focus and navigation system for iPhone and iPad. You can browse and interact entirely with a controller or keyboard.
- Hold Command or the controller’s Select button to view the shortcut cheatsheet.
- A unified navigation bar for more consistent browsing and editing.
- Many long-press and hidden actions have been replaced with more conventional, iOS-style interactions.
- Batch management and actions.
- Adaptive rotation throughout the app.
- Controllers can be assigned to a player slot. On cores that expect a keyboard, controller inputs can be mapped to keyboard events.

### Features

Library and Artwork

- Covers now support separate icon and banner artwork. Box art is used in regular lists, icons in square layouts, and banners as the landscape focus backdrop.
- Online artwork from Libretro Thumbnails and SteamGridDB (Grids / Heroes / Logos / Icons; SteamGridDB requires your own API key).
- Switching platform or category rematches cover art.

Game Data

- Game metadata: auto-match, search the database, or edit it yourself (developer, publisher, series, genre, release date, region, overview, and more).
- ESRB ratings and matching icons. Rating icons can be hidden in Settings.
- A redesigned save-state manager with import and export.
- Scoped settings: the same option can be stored at game, platform, or global level, and each can be cleared or reset independently.
- batch scraping for covers, icons, and banners.
- 

Shaders and Skins

- Real-time shader preview, without loading the shader first.
- Redesigned default GBA skin.
- Flex skins now support customizing button size and position.

Achievements, Cheats, and Netplay

- RetroAchievements pages are easier to read and load faster.
- MultiSet support: earn subset achievements without a patched ROM. Switching the achievement list only changes what is shown; it does not affect which sets you can unlock while playing.
- Online cheat database: search, multi-select add, and bookmarks.
- Netplay for many Libretro cores: host or join a room, public lobby, LAN scan, relay, spectator mode, and room password. Your Adventurer Card nickname is used as the Netplay display name. You can now trade treasured Pokémon with friends over the network, or go head-to-head on arcade systems.
- Rewind: add it to the shortcut menu, a controller mapping, or TriggerPro, then touch and hold to use it.

Advanced Features and Import

- Core Settings: intended for advanced users. Incorrect values may prevent games from launching. Settings can be reset per game or per platform.
- Settings now include an Adventurer Card, with a customizable nickname and avatar.
- Import games from DukeX.
- Import games from Armsx2.
- PS1 now supports importing `.bin` files directly.


### New Systems and Cores

Symbian (EKA2L1)

- Supports S60v1, N-Gage 1.0, S60v2, S60v3, N-Gage 2.0, S60v5, and Symbian^3.
- Touch input, firmware management, and system apps.
- Legacy / PPL / TXM JIT.

PC Engine (Beetle PCE)

- Supports TurboGrafx-16, TurboGrafx-CD, and SuperGrafx, with subcategory switching.

Neo Geo Pocket / Color (Beetle NeoPop)

- Supports Neo Geo Pocket and Neo Geo Pocket Color, with subcategory switching.

Commodore 64 (VICE x64sc)

- Full keyboard support, with switching between gamepad and keyboard skins.

Amiga (PUAE)

- Full keyboard support, with switching between gamepad and keyboard skins.

GameCube / Wii (Dolphin)

- Legacy / PPL / TXM JIT.
- Wii: Wiimote sideways mode.
- Dolphin cheats, including Action Replay Max decryption.
- Wiimote skins for Wii

Other Cores

- Mesen-S added for SNES / GB / GBC.
- gpSP added for GBA, and can be switched with mGBA and VBA-M.

### JIT Fixes and Improvements

- Fixed JIT failing on TXM devices running iOS 26.6 and later.
- Revised TXM device detection.
- N64 GLideN64 and ParaLLEl RDP now both support JIT.

### Core Updates

The following cores have been updated to the latest upstream stable releases.

- 3DS (Azahar, Citra)
- PS1 (Beetle PSX HW)
- DOS (DOSBox Pure)
- Dreamcast (Flycast) — see the save-state migration note above
- NDS (melonDS)
- PSP (PPSSPP)
- N64 (Mupen64Plus)

### Fixes

- Numerous bug fixes and performance optimizations

data.name: v1.9.0
data.body:
• Added JAVA (J2ME) support
> Includes two cores: J2meJS (based on Mozilla’s PluotSorbet) and freej2me (based on CheerpJ)
> J2meJS supports fast-forward
> J2meJS runs natively, offering improved performance and compatibility
> J2meJS provides limited network access
> J2meJS includes partial M3G support
> freej2me relies on CheerpJ (requires an internet connection)
> Automatically detects JAR resolution, with manual override available in J2ME settings
> Support touchscreen version JAR apps
> Screen scaling options available (stretch or fit)
        
• Added MS-DOS support (powered by DOSBox-Pure)
> Built-in gamepad and keyboard skins
> Game screen can be used as a touchpad for mouse input
> Added “Insert Disc” option for multi-disc workflows
> Full DOSBox-Pure configuration available in both settings and in-game

• Added DOOM support (powered by prboom)
• Added XeniOS Link, allowing you to launch and manage your XeniOS library directly within Manic EMU
• Added skin button sound effects support (by including CAF audio files in custom skins; can be toggled in Settings - Skin Sound Effects)
• Fixed multiple issues caused by incorrect file paths on macOS
• Fixed an issue where multi-file ROMs were not uploaded during iCloud sync
• Fixed an issue where multi-line cheat codes did not work
• Fixed incorrect C button mapping for MCD and 32X
• Fixed an issue where UI could not be controlled via external controllers on iOS 26.3.1
• Various other fixes and improvements

J2ME support in Manic EMU is made possible thanks to the outstanding work of @zixing131 (紫星) and @Rosabis. Their development of J2meJS laid the foundation for this feature. With their improvements, Manic achieves better MIDP compatibility and even supports M3G, which is essential for bringing J2ME into the Manic ecosystem.

Special thanks to @StephenDev0 (developer of StikDebug) for contributions to DOOM core integration.

Special thanks to @cocorograph-kaz for multiple fixes and contributions.

data.title: Feat: Adding RomM Support
data.body:
# Summary

This PR adds RomM Integration with ManicEMU. 

_**As both a RomM user and ManicEMU user - I saw #52 and figured I would add it.**_ 

## Scope of Changes
This Pull Request Includes the following changes:

### RomM is now listed as a new Local Network Provider
- Users can now add their own RomM instance

### ROMs can now be downloaded through RomM
- Users are able to view all consoles and download ROM for each console via the UI 
  - There is no support added for importing BIOS files 

### Save State Synchronization
- Users will have their save states synchronized both to and from RomM. This happens in one of four ways:
  - On application load (Toggle-able in the settings)
  - On game exit (Toggle-able in the settings)
  - After importing a ROM.
  - Manual sync button on the game menu
    - This button does **not** show up if a RomM instance is not setup
- Save state conflict will prompt the user to resolve (either by keeping the device state or remote state)

## Limitations

- If a ROM  is not found in your RomM instance (via a hash comparison), then you will not be able to sync any save states for that particular ROM

## Testing

This feature was tested on an `iPhone 17 pro max` running `iOS 27 Developer Beta 2`. The following scenarios were tested:

- Adding a RomM instance 
- Downloading a ROM from RomM
- Playing a ROM downloaded from RomM
- Manually syncing a save state created from the device
- Manually syncing to bring a save from the RomM instance
- Toggling syncing on application load
- Toggling syncing on ROM exit
- Syncing saves for a ROM downloaded from a different source (but where the hash matches a hash of a ROM of RomM)

data.title: fix(cheat): use '+' separator for libretro cheats and fix auto-detect logic
data.body:
## Summary
- Replace newline separators with `+` (libretro standard) when sending multi-line cheats to cores
- Fix auto-detect format loop that returned `nil` after first non-matching format

## Bug 1: Cheat separator mismatch (all libretro cores)

`CheatFormat.formatted(with:)` joins multi-line cheats with `\n`, but all libretro cores expect `+` as the multi-line separator.

**Example** (SNES Game Genie):
- ManicEmu sends: `ABCD-EFGH\nIJKL-MNOP`
- Core expects: `ABCD-EFGH+IJKL-MNOP`
- Result: decode failure, cheat silently ignored

This affects **all libretro-based systems**: SNES, PS1, N64, Genesis, Saturn, etc.

### Fix
```diff
 // PlayViewController.swift line 2236
-LibretroCore.sharedInstance().addCheatCode(cheatCode.code, ...)
+let coreCode = cheatCode.code.replacingOccurrences(of: "\n", with: "+")
+LibretroCore.sharedInstance().addCheatCode(String(coreCode), ...)
```

## Bug 2: Auto-detect only checks first format

`AddCheatCodeView.checkCheat()` returned `nil` on the first non-matching format instead of continuing the loop:

### Fix
```diff
 if isMatchThisFormat {
     return (formatString, cheatFormat)
-} else {
-    return nil
 }
+// Loop continues to try next format
```

## Test plan
- [ ] Enter a multi-line Game Genie cheat for SNES — verify it takes effect
- [ ] Enter a GameShark cheat for PS1 — verify it takes effect
- [ ] Enter a Pro Action Replay cheat for Genesis — verify it takes effect
- [ ] Use auto-detect with a PAR code when Game Genie is listed first — verify it is correctly detected
- [ ] Single-line cheats still work (no regression)

Closes #47

data.title: feat: add prboom libretro core for Doom support
data.body:
## Added prboom libretro core for Doom support

There is an age-old question in tech:

**"Can it run Doom?"**

With this PR, the answer for **Manic Emulator** is now **yes**.

This adds the **prboom libretro core**, giving Manic Emulator support for **Doom**, **Doom II**, and compatible WADs/mods. It may not solve every problem in life, but it does solve one very important one.

Manic Emulator can now proudly join the long tradition of hardware and software projects whose value is measured, at least in part, by whether they can run Doom.

## What this PR does

- Adds the **prboom libretro core**
- Enables support for **Doom** and **Doom II**
- Supports compatible WADs and many related mods
- Keeps changes focused on what is needed for this feature

## Why

Because at some point, every platform must face the ultimate test.

Now Manic Emulator has.

data.title: fix(sync): upload companion files for multi-file ROMs to iCloud
data.body:
## Summary
- Upload companion files (.bin, .img, .sub, etc.) to iCloud when importing multi-file ROMs

## Problem
When importing a multi-file ROM (e.g., PS1 `.cue` + `.bin`), only the main file (`.cue`) was uploaded to iCloud. The companion files (`.bin` track data) were copied locally but `SyncManager.upload()` was never called for them.

This caused other devices to sync only the `.cue` file with no actual game data — the game could not launch on the synced device.

### Before (broken)
```swift
// FilesImporter.swift line 515 — only main file uploaded
SyncManager.upload(localFilePath: game.romUrl.path)  // .cue only
// ❌ .bin files silently skipped
```

### After (fixed)
```swift
SyncManager.upload(localFilePath: game.romUrl.path)
// ✅ Upload companion files (.bin, .img, .sub, etc.)
if items.count > 0 {
    let romParentPath = game.romUrl.path.deletingLastPathComponent
    for item in items {
        SyncManager.upload(localFilePath: romParentPath.appendingPathComponent(item.lastPathComponent))
    }
}
```

The fix is applied to both code paths:
1. **New game import** (line ~515) — when a game is first added
2. **Existing game restore** (line ~439) — when ROM files are re-imported for an existing database entry

Note: The **delete** logic already correctly handles multi-file ROMs via `SyncManager.deletePath(localPath: romParentPath)` which removes the entire directory.

## Affected systems
| System | Main file | Companion files (previously not synced) |
|--------|-----------|----------------------------------------|
| PS1 | `.cue` | `.bin` (one or more tracks) |
| Saturn | `.cue` | `.bin` |
| Mega CD | `.cue` | `.bin` |
| Dreamcast | `.gdi` | `.bin` (track files) |
| Any | `.ccd` | `.img`, `.sub` |

## Test plan
- [ ] Import a PS1 game (.cue + .bin) on device A, verify .bin files appear in iCloud
- [ ] Sync to device B, verify the game launches successfully
- [ ] Import a multi-disc game (.m3u + multiple .cue/.bin), verify all files sync
- [ ] Verify single-file ROMs (.chd, .pbp) still work correctly (no regression)

Closes #42

data.title: fix(macOS): resolve BIOS path correctly on macOS
data.body:
## Summary
- Fix `libretroPath` in `StringExtensions.swift` to use `.backwards` option when matching `/Library/`, so it matches the app's Library directory instead of the user's `~/Library` on macOS

## Problem
On macOS, the sandbox container path contains `/Library/` twice:
```
/Users/X/Library/Containers/{UUID}/Data/Library/Libretro/system
         ^^^^^^^^ (1st match — wrong)              ^^^^^^^^ (correct)
```

`String.range(of: "/Library/")` matched the **first** occurrence, producing:
```
~/Library/Containers/{UUID}/Data/Library/Libretro/system
```

This path is written to `retroarch.cfg` as `system_directory`. Since RetroArch's C backend does not expand `~` for this setting, the Beetle PSX HW core receives a literal path that doesn't exist → **"Firmware is missing: scph5500.bin"** error.

On iOS, this works correctly because the container path only contains `/Library/` once.

## Fix
```diff
- if let range = self.range(of: "/Documents/") ?? self.range(of: "/Library/") {
+ if let range = self.range(of: "/Documents/") ?? self.range(of: "/Library/", options: .backwards) {
```

Using `.backwards` ensures the **last** `/Library/` is matched (the app's Library), producing the correct path:
```
~/Library/Libretro/system ✅
```

## Test plan
- [ ] Verify PS1 games launch on macOS with imported BIOS (scph5500.bin / ps1_rom.bin)
- [ ] Verify PS1 games still launch on iOS (no regression)
- [ ] Verify other systems using Libretro cores work on macOS (PPSSPP, 3DS, etc.)

Closes #40

data.title: Add N64 JIT support with GlideN64 via StikDebug on iOS 26
data.body:
## Summary

Adds ARM64 dynamic recompiler (JIT) support for N64 emulation using the mupen64plus-next core with GlideN64 rendering on iOS. Requires StikDebug for JIT memory page preparation on iOS 26 (TXM).

## What's Included

### N64 JIT Core (`mupen64plus.next.jit.libretro.framework`)
- Pre-built from [mupen64plus-libretro-nx](https://github.com/libretro/mupen64plus-libretro-nx) with `make platform=ios-arm64-jit`
- Key build flags: `WITH_DYNAREC=aarch64`, `GLES3=1`, `-DIOS_DYNAREC_JIT`, `-DDOUBLE_CACHE_ADDR_IOS`
- GlideN64 (OpenGL ES 3) + HLE RSP only — Parallel-RDP/RSP explicitly disabled (`HAVE_PARALLEL_RDP=0`)
- CPU mode forced to `EMUMODE_DYNAREC` at compile time

### iOS JIT Memory Model (W^X Dual-Mapping)
The dynarec allocates a 32 MB code cache using a dual-mapping approach to comply with Apple's W^X policy:
1. `mmap()` an RX (read+execute) region
2. `BRK #0x69` — StikDebug intercepts this, reads x0 (address) and x1 (size), calls `prepare_memory_region` to make pages executable via the TXM debug proxy
3. `vm_remap()` creates a second virtual mapping (RW alias) of the same physical pages
4. Dynarec **writes** generated ARM64 code through `base_addr` (RW) and the CPU **executes** from `base_addr_rx` (RX)

### Apple ARM64 ABI Compliance
- x18 reserved as platform register (never allocated to guest registers)
- Block linking disabled (code cache at unpredictable ASLR address)
- Mach-O assembly linkage port (`_` prefix, `@PAGE/@PAGEOFF`, `.globl` exports)
- x16 used as trampoline register instead of x18
- `sys_cache_control(kCacheFunctionPrepareForExecution)` for dual-mapping-aware cache flush

### StikDebug Script (`Scripts/StikDebug/manic.js`)
Custom iOS 26 TXM JIT script for StikDebug that:
- Runs in infinite loop mode (stays connected)
- Intercepts `BRK #0x69` breakpoints from the dynarec
- Calls `prepare_memory_region` to mark JIT code cache as executable
- Advances PC+4 to resume execution
- Handles `BRK #0x70`/`#0x71` debug breakpoints
- Includes diagnostic logging for non-breakpoint exceptions with register dumps and region tracking

### App Integration
- **Game.swift**: Selects JIT or interpreter framework based on per-game `jit` flag
- **PlayViewController**: `applyN64CoreConfig` sets cpucore/rdp-plugin/rsp-plugin; explicitly sets `video_driver=gl` for GlideN64 (prevents stale vulkan config from persisting); removed dylib probe (`dlopen`/`dlclose` cycle before real load was causing black screen)
- **GameInfoDetailReusableView**: JIT toggle visible for N64 even without active debugger (allows pre-enabling before StikDebug attaches)
- **N64.swift**: C-stick mapped as proper analog axis
- **Xcode project**: Embeds `mupen64plus.next.jit.libretro.framework`

### Controller Support
- Custom `manic` joypad driver replaces MFi for direct button state passing
- `input_driver.c`: Fast path for manic driver bypassing RetroArch bind lookups
- `input_autodetect_builtin.c`: Manic controller autodetect entry
- DeltaCore: `acceptsControllerInput` guard prevents input during init/pause, playerIndex fallback to 0

### Other
- MoltenVK bundle loading fallbacks in `vulkan_common.c`
- ResourcesKit: Force resource refresh when System.core bundle size changes
- Runtime N64 plugin introspection (rdp/rsp/parallel status via dlsym)

## How to Build the JIT Core

```bash
cd mupen64plus-libretro-nx
make clean
make platform=ios-arm64-jit -j$(sysctl -n hw.ncpu)
cp mupen64plus_next_libretro_ios.dylib \
   /path/to/ManicEMU/Cores/mupen64plus.next.jit.libretro.framework/mupen64plus.next.jit.libretro
```

## Battery Impact
Testing shows JIT uses ~15-20% less battery per minute vs interpreter (0.17%/min vs 0.21%/min).

## Requirements
- iOS 15.0+
- StikDebug with `manic.js` script for JIT memory preparation
- The `manic.js` script is included at `Scripts/StikDebug/manic.js`
